mental_model: It is a growable partition of memref values into may-alias groups: every memref starts alone in its own group, and each proven alias pair merges the two groups, so any later 'do these two names touch the same memory?' question is one equivalence lookup.
need: Consumers need a transitive may-alias relation over SSA values, but the IR only offers local evidence (this cast's result is its source); someone must accumulate that evidence into a queryable form.
responsibility: Own the alias equivalence relation for one analysis scope: seed it with every memref value, absorb alias evidence pair by pair, and answer may-alias queries.
observable_outcome: After setup, isAlias(v1, v2) returns true exactly when a chain of recorded alias pairs connects the two values — observable as grouped alias sets in the debug dump.

audience_contract.who: compiler engineers who know SSA values and memrefs but have not read this utility
audience_contract.assumed_knowledge: SSA values, memref types, what 'may alias' means
audience_contract.not_assumed: llvm::EquivalenceClasses internals, this codebase's alias-source list

triggers.interaction: constructs the state over the root function at analysis time, unions every alias pair found by getOperationAliasInfo, then queries isAlias while scanning dependencies

upstream.interaction: supplies (result, source) alias pairs for cast/view/select-style ops

downstream.interaction: uses isAlias as the predicate that decides whether two memory ops conflict

inputs.name: scope operation
inputs.form: Operation* whose memref-typed results and block arguments are seeded
inputs.description: given once at construction; defines the query domain

inputs.name: alias evidence pairs
inputs.description: fed by the consumer from getOperationAliasInfo

outputs.name: may-alias answers
outputs.description: equivalence query over the accumulated relation

outputs.name: debug dump

mechanism.summary: Three phases across its lifetime: seed one singleton class per memref value by walking the scope; absorb alias evidence by merging the two values' classes (memref-only guard); answer queries as equivalence checks over the merged classes.

stages.name: Seed
stages.what: walk the scope op; insert every memref-typed op result and block argument as its own class

stages.name: Absorb
stages.what: unionAliasSets(v1, v2): refuse non-memref pairs, otherwise unionSets merges the two classes transitively

stages.name: Query
stages.what: isAlias(v1, v2) = isEquivalent over the merged classes; printAlias lists leader/member sets for debugging

control_flow: consumer drives everything: construct → union loop over alias pairs → query inside its own dependency scan; the class never acts on its own
data_flow: evidence flows one way: view/cast/select ops → getOperationAliasInfo pairs → unionAliasSets → aliasInfo classes → isAlias answers

implementation_view.description: llvm::EquivalenceClasses<Value> — a union-find over SSA values; the class is a thin, type-guarded facade over it
two compile-time variants selected by __LLVM_MAJOR_VERSION_22_COMPATIBLE__ (member_iterator types, print loops) — introduced by the llvm-22 fix commit
state is constructed per analysis (MergeVecScope builds one per runOnOperation call), lives on the pass stack frame, and dies with it — no shared or cached state

conceptual_view.description: the value of union-find is the transitive closure: after A∪B and B∪C, isAlias(A,C) is true without storing the pair — exactly what a may-alias relation needs
the memref-only guard keeps the relation total and closed: non-memref values never enter, so queries outside the seeded domain answer 'not equivalent' rather than crashing or lying

provenance.source: RECONSTRUCTED from the observed dump (EV-106) and the seeding/union code (EV-102/EV-103); member names symbolic

canonical_example.initial_state: scope with memrefs {arg0, subview(arg0), buf} — three singleton classes {arg0}, {subview}, {buf}
important_states: class count drops 3 → 2 when the union lands
canonical_example.result: equivalence query reflects the merged set — matching the observed grouped dump where subview and its block-argument source share one leader

state_transitions.operation: walk scope; insert each memref value
state_transitions.after: one singleton class per memref value
state_transitions.reason: every value starts aliasing only itself

state_transitions.before: {subview(arg0)} and {arg0} as separate classes; allocs/call results singletons
state_transitions.after: one class {subview, arg0}; unrelated values untouched (allocs stay singletons)
state_transitions.reason: recorded evidence that the subview reads/writes its source's memory
the relation is defined over memrefs only

decisions.question: Should this pair join the relation?
decisions.reason: keeps the relation closed over the seeded memref domain

contracts.element: alias pairs must already be memref-typed values from the seeded scope (else the union is a silent no-op)
isAlias(v1, v2) predicate and printAlias() debug listing

constraints.statement: union partners must both be memref-typed (mixed pairs are silently ignored)
query domain is exactly the seeded set: values never inserted behave as unrelated singletons

invariants.statement: alias classes are always a partition of the seeded memref values (EquivalenceClasses guarantee)

boundaries.statement: accumulate-and-query may-alias over memref values with transitive closure

alias evidence only enters when a consumer feeds it: the class performs no flow/pointer analysis of its own, and there is no dedicated unit test pinning its behavior (covered only indirectly through merge fixtures)

placement.why_here: a stateful helper next to its alias-evidence producer (HIVM Utils) and consumed by analysis passes; it is deliberately not a pass so several consumers could reuse it
placement.why_not_earlier: there is nothing to accumulate before an analysis scope exists — the class is constructed per scope
placement.why_not_later: queries must be available while the consumer's dependency scan runs, not after it

key_takeaways: A union-find over SSA values: seed every memref, merge on alias evidence, query by equivalence.
The consumer owns the evidence loop; the class only accumulates and answers — it does no analysis of its own.
The memref-only guard keeps the relation closed; mixed-type unions are silent no-ops.
Currently single-consumer (MergeVecScope) with no dedicated unit test; behavior is pinned only indirectly by merge fixtures.

class.responsibility: accumulate the memref may-alias relation for one analysis scope
class.lifecycle: constructed on the consumer's stack per analysis run; no copy/destroy semantics beyond RAII; dies with the consumer's scope
